eos_records.label: Reynard et al. (1996), BM3, ruby pressure scale
eos_records.notes: This is the ruby-pressure assignment of the same 16-row compression/decompression experiment represented by the companion ice-VII-scale record. It is a distinct fit, not a duplicate parameter transcription. The paper reports that V0 was varied and stayed within 0.01% of the measured in-cell value, while K0 was fixed at the adopted 212 GPa Brillouin value. Ruby-line broadening above 15 GPa showed increasing nonhydrostatic stress; the authors therefore regarded K0'=7.5 as less realistic than the ice-VII-scale result. The source gives neither parameter covariance nor a confidence convention for parenthesized fit errors, and it does not specify an exact ruby calibration equation. The numerical 298 K reference encodes the source's qualitative 'ambient temperature' wording rather than a measured sample temperature.

eos_records.label: Reynard et al. (1996), preferred BM3, ice-VII pressure scale
eos_records.notes: This is the authors' preferred pressure assignment of the same experiment represented by the companion ruby-scale record. It is a distinct fit, not a duplicate parameter transcription. Ice-VII (110) diffraction and MgSiO3 ilmenite were measured on the same 50 micrometer X-ray spot; Table 1 prints 12 finite-pressure Pi values, and Figure 3f additionally plots the two ambient measurements as zero-pressure anchors, giving 14 usable rows. The paper reports that V0 was varied and K0 was fixed at the adopted 212 GPa Brillouin value. Above 15 GPa the pressure medium developed nonhydrostatic stress and pressure gradients; the bracketed ice-pressure quantities are maximum gradient estimates, not stated one-sigma errors. The source gives neither parameter covariance nor a confidence convention for fitted-parameter errors. The numerical 298 K reference encodes the source's qualitative 'ambient temperature' wording rather than a measured sample temperature.

eos_records.label: Shi et al. (2022), selected BM3-MGD corundum model 3
eos_records.notes: Published corundum model 3 selected in main Table 1 and Supporting Information Table S3: a third-order Birch-Murnaghan 300 K reference isotherm plus Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. The prose calls the cold term Murnaghan, but Equation 2 is algebraically BM3; fixed K0'=4 makes its cold curve numerically BM2. Equations 3-6 define Delta Pth=gamma/V [E_D(V,T)-E_D(V,300 K)], gamma=gamma0(V/V0)^q, and theta=theta0 exp[-(gamma-gamma0)/q], with n=5 atoms per Al2O3 formula unit. V0=255.1 A^3 is the fixed conventional six-formula-unit hexagonal corundum cell from Lutterotti and Scardi (1990); K0, gamma0, and q were fitted, while K0', V0, theta0, Tr, and n were fixed. Main Table 1 reports K0=246(2) GPa for the selected model, whereas sensitivity Table 2 reports 246(1) GPa; the selected-table uncertainty is retained and the discrepancy is explicit. Table 2's 500 K and 800 K Debye-temperature trials are sensitivity fits, not additional preferred records. All 75 Table S1 observations are bundled: 59 are grouped under Pt pressures (including the fixed 0 GPa reference row) and 16 under NaCl pressures. The source does not state an uncertainty confidence convention or coefficient covariance matrix. An independent unweighted Peritheos fit of pressure residuals at all 75 printed V-T states, with the published fixed parameters, returns K0=246.3083 GPa, gamma0=1.35931, and q=0.800868; all reproduce the published coefficients within their reported uncertainties. The published curve has a 1.23305 GPa pressure RMSE and the refit has a 1.19139 GPa RMSE. Weighting by the tabulated coordinate uncertainties does not recover q, so the parity result is specifically identified as an unweighted pressure-residual reproduction rather than an undocumented reconstruction of the authors' weighting.

eos_records.label: Shi et al. (2022), selected BM3-MGD model 2
eos_records.notes: Published model 2 selected in main Table 1 and reused in Supporting Information Table S3: a third-order Birch-Murnaghan 300 K reference isotherm plus Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. The prose calls the cold term Murnaghan, but Equation 2 is algebraically BM3; fixed K0'=4 makes its cold curve numerically BM2. Equations 3-6 define Delta Pth=gamma/V [E_D(V,T)-E_D(V,300 K)], gamma=gamma0(V/V0)^q, and theta=theta0 exp[-(gamma-gamma0)/q], with n=5 atoms per formula unit. V0=165.2(7) A^3 is the conventional four-formula-unit Pbcn cell, fitted by extrapolation from high-pressure data rather than measured at ambient conditions. K0, V0, theta0, and gamma0 were fitted; K0'=4 and q=1 were fixed. Parenthetical errors are retained as generic published uncertainties because no confidence convention or covariance matrix is given. Table 3 also reports four q-sensitivity fits (q=0.6, 1.4, 1.8, and 2.2); they are documented alternatives, not separate preferred EOS records. The article states a 153 GPa, 3400 K EOS scope. Table S2 nevertheless prints two identical 156.7(4.0) GPa, 3670(370) K Rh2O3(II) volumes at the reported onset of CaIrO3-type Al2O3; they remain in the source dataset with an explicit phase-context flag but do not extend this record's declared validity. At the Table S2 state V=129.8 A^3 and T=300 K, the stored model gives 100.1123 GPa versus 100.0(1.0) GPa. Across all 75 printed rows it gives a 1.1434 GPa pressure RMSE. The independent errors-in-variables refit is reported in docs/literature-reproductions.md and the primary-EOS refit ledger.

eos_records.label: Sokolova et al. (2013), Holzapfel thermal model (2016 workbook)
eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

name: B4C

eos_records.label: Somayazulu et al. (2023), BM3 + MGD
eos_records.notes: Third-order Birch-Murnaghan reference isotherm plus Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. The room-temperature quench-data fit gives K0=221(2) GPa and K0'=3.3(1) with V0=328.4 A^3 fixed; those three reference parameters were then fixed in the P-V-T fit. The official supplement defines T0=298 K, theta0=1425 K, n=5 atoms per B4C formula unit, gamma(V)=gamma0*(V/V0)^q, and theta(V)=theta0*exp[(gamma0-gamma(V))/q]. With a=1, the paper's generalized Tange relation reduces exactly to this integrated constant-q MGD model. The final article reports gamma0=0.8 fixed and q=2.1 varied. At the 41 heated supplementary points' printed V and T, the published parameterization gives a pressure RMSE of 1.39 GPa and chi-squared per observation of 0.961. A Peritheos P-V-T errors-in-variables refit with gamma0 fixed gives q=1.050(519), so it does not independently recover q=2.1; details and the primary-data transcription are in docs/literature-reproductions.md. The average disordered R-3m structure is diffraction-ready and is reported stable over the experimental range.

eos_records.notes: The paper calls this the Berman P-V-T fit. EosFit7 implements the Berman reference volume as the truncated quadratic V0(T)=V0*[1+alpha0*(T-Tr)+0.5*alpha1*(T-Tr)^2], with K0(T)=K0+dK0/dT*(T-Tr). EosFit7c varied alpha0=1.94(16)e-5 K^-1 and dK0/dT=-0.008(3) GPa/K while alpha1=0.0573e-8 K^-2 and the 300 K BM3 parameters were fixed. The article's displayed exponential-integral equation instead describes EosFit's Fei-style exact integration and is inconsistent with its Berman label. The implied BM3 K0''=-0.0166 GPa^-1 is derived rather than an independent parameter. Reproduction diagnostics compare both EosFit effective-variance and Peritheos errors-in-variables objectives.

eos_records.notes: Static-lattice 0 K DFT parameterization of the ideal cubic Pm-3m (Glazer a0a0a0) CaSiO3 perovskite branch. The paper finds this branch dynamically unstable at all investigated pressures, so this is a theoretical reference curve and not a stable ambient phase. Table 2 reports V0/Z; Pm-3m has Z=1, so 44.579 A^3 is also the conventional cubic-cell volume (a0=3.54577 A). All three BM3 coefficients were fitted; no parameter uncertainties, covariance, fit weights, or underlying E(V) rows are published. The Table 2 footnote estimates calculation uncertainty as about 20 meV per molecule, an energy-scale estimate rather than an EOS-coefficient error. The distinct Pm-3m BM4 fit and all eight phase-specific low-symmetry BM3/BM4 pairs are now represented as executable sibling records on the appropriate material cards.

notes: The stated FPMD sampling spans approximately 0-150 GPa; Table 1 publishes fitted isochors from 1000 to 4000 K and V/V0=0.70-1.00.

Section 2 prints a computational temperature range of 300-1500 K, but Figure 2 explicitly labels calculated FPMD points at 1000, 2000, 3000, and 4000 K. The paper warns that the very-low-pressure, high-temperature corner lies outside cubic CaSiO3 stability or near melting, so this rectangular numerical envelope is not a phase-stability guarantee.

eos_records.notes: Preferred Vinet reference isotherm plus a constant-q Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure relative to 1000 K. The integrated Debye-temperature law follows equations 4-10 of Tange et al. (2009), which Kawai and Tsuchiya explicitly adopt; n=5 for one CaSiO3 formula unit. V0 is already one cubic Pm-3m conventional cell because Z=1. The input stresses came from LDA-PWSCF NVT FPMD on an 80-atom 2x2x1 tetragonal-supercell representation constrained to cubic metrics, with 50 Ry cutoff, a 2x2x2 k-point grid, 1 fs steps, 1 ps equilibration, and 5 ps production averages. Figure 1 reports a convergence benchmark near 15 GPa and 2000 K: the 2x2x2 sampling gives diagonal stresses 15.3, 15.5, and 15.2 GPa, compared with 16.0, 16.1, and 14.6 GPa at Gamma only; no volume is printed, so this is not an EOS-fit row. No parameter uncertainties or covariance are reported, so missing errors are null rather than zero. The alternate BM3 column is intentionally not added because this contribution is limited to one literature EOS record and the article plots and abstracts the Vinet result. The abstract's K0=203.95 GPa reproduces Table 1 (for example 184.42 GPa rounds to 184.5 GPa at V/V0=0.70 and 4000 K), whereas the PDF-extracted Table 2 value 203.5 GPa predicts 184.06 GPa; the benchmark-consistent abstract value is retained. Section 2's printed 300-1500 K simulation range conflicts with calculated 1000-4000 K points in Figure 2 and cannot be resolved without the raw state table.

eos_records.label: Sokolova et al. (2013), Holzapfel thermal model (2016 workbook)
eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

eos_records.label: Fratanduono et al. (2020), Cu 298 K third-order Vinet

notes: The ramp measurements reach 2.30 TPa; fcc diffraction is observed to 1.15 TPa. Neither is an exact published 298 K isotherm fit interval, so no isothermal pressure validity interval is inferred.

eos_records.notes: Central 298 K isotherm row of Table I, using Supplemental S4 Eq. (2). The nearby main-text prose says 300 K, but Table I and S4 explicitly specify 298 K. rho0=8.939 g/cm3 is a prescribed reference density without a reported uncertainty. V0 is converted with 63.546 g/mol and four Cu atoms per conventional fcc cell; the material-card lattice is not substituted for this record reference state. Table S1 contains reduced-isentrope observations, not 298 K isothermal rows. No numerical 298 K fit dataset, weights, coefficient covariance, or confidence level for the Table I coefficient errors is published in the inspected article and supplement. The upper/lower isotherm rows describe separate envelope fits, not coefficient errors or independent 298 K observations. A refit of the published 298 K EOS is not possible with the current information. Fratanduono explicitly describes the Gruneisen prescription for reducing measured stress to the principal isentrope, but does not explicitly specify the Debye isentrope-to-298 K calculation used in our diagnostic. Applying Kraus (2016) Eq. (16), its Debye caloric model, and theta0=343.5 K is our inference, not a confirmed reproduction of the 2020 reduction. The 53 candidate points also use an unconfirmed graphical Hugoniot input and omit 46 higher-compression rows. Their 1.562 GPa RMS agreement with the published curve does not establish recovery of the original data, coefficient parity, or a superior EOS.

eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

eos_records.label: Correa et al. (2008), logarithmic-moment double-Debye Helmholtz

notes: The lower volume is the compressed diamond phonon-DOS state in Figure 3; the cold curve itself was fitted over approximately 1-9 A^3/atom.
The upper pressure is the calculated 0 K diamond-BC8 crossing. These are marginal model bounds, not a phase-stability surface at finite temperature.

eos_records.notes: Complete diamond free-energy branch from equations 2-18; the double-Debye weights conserve the logarithmic phonon moment theta_0 (equation 13). Table I volumes are per atom; the public API uses A^3 per eight-atom conventional diamond cell and converts internally to J bar^-1 mol^-1 of atoms. The Vinet term is a motionless-ion DFT-GGA cold curve. The authors state that its theoretical V0 is about 3% too large after zero-point and thermal effects and may need an application-specific density shift; Peritheos preserves the published value. The constant anharmonic coefficient changes caloric properties but contributes no pressure. Electronic excitations are neglected for insulating diamond as in the source. Factor-of-two source ambiguity: Correa equation 18 defines F_anh=-a*T^2 with a=3.8e-5 K^-1, whereas Benedict 2014 says it carries over the same correction but writes F_anh=-alpha*T^2/2 and tabulates alpha=3.79e-5 K^-1. This record follows Correa literally; in Benedict's normalization the equivalent coefficient would be alpha=2*a. The source reports no coefficient uncertainties or covariance.

source.coordinate_transform: The source uses the P21nm subgroup origin and prints Fe=(0,0.25,0), H=(0.5,0.25,0), O1=(0.348,0.485,0), and O2=(0.651,0.015,0). source.notes: The diffraction structure is the 50 GPa static Pnnm low-spin calculation of Insixiengmay and Stixrude (2023). eos_records.label: Campbell et al. (2009), B1 FeO, 295 K BM3-Debye
eos_records.notes: Equation (5) and Table 1: 295 K BM3 plus Mie-Gruneisen-Debye, gamma=gamma0*(V/V0)^q and theta=theta0*(V/V0)^(-gamma(V)). No explicit electronic or anharmonic pressure. Source molar V0 is converted to the Z=4 conventional cell using exact SI Avogadro constant. Italicized Table 1 values are held fixed, and nonitalic values with errors are fitted. The confidence convention and covariance of published errors are not specified. Temperature-corrected workbook values are used as printed; no second correction is applied. The published fit also includes Seagle et al. (2008). Its 81 V-T rows are linked, but exact row-wise pressures and Campbell recalibration are not published. Independent refits therefore report a current-study subset and a nominal-isobar sensitivity reconstruction. The starting Fe1-xO powder equilibrates with metallic Fe; Sections 2.1, 3 and 5 explicitly identify the selected oxide as stoichiometric Fe1.00O in B1, not Fe0.94O, rhombohedral wustite or B8. Stoichiometry follows the Stolen-Grønvold model-B field (above 5 GPa at 900 K, boundary slope below -120 K/GPa), not a direct per-row chemical assay.

assessment.basis: Conditional reproduction, not an exact recovery of the unpublished regression protocol. Campbell specifies least squares but no residual variable, weights, covariance, or final row mask. The main diagnostic uses equal pressure-residual weights and simultaneous fitting of the three Table 1 free parameters. Fe/FeO main fits use current-study Table S2 only: Seagle contributes 81 recoverable V-T pairs but no individual pressures or NaCl observations. Separate sensitivities reconstruct 65 hcp-calibrated pressures using benchmark-checked Seagle (2006), compare its conflicting reference volumes, and optionally retain 16 unresolved rows as nominal-isobar estimates. A separate protocol audit adds 14 conditional fcc pressures from Funamori/Boehler/Basinski, leaving only two missing-iron-volume rows without individual pressures. The exact historical fcc reduction and combined regression remain unresolved. These are derived pressures, not original row-level pressure data. The published Fe/FeO records are deferred from the executable catalog because the combined-data mismatch remains unresolved. No refitted coefficients replace the source records. See literature-reproductions/campbell-2009-buffers.md.

eos_records.label: B8 Fe0.94O, Fischer et al. (2011)
eos_records.notes: Fischer et al. report a thermal EOS for iron-saturated FeO, not a standalone 300 K BM3. The Fe0.94O starting powder was mixed with Fe and the authors treat the equilibrated high-P-T oxide as approximately stoichiometric FeO. Reported sample temperatures already include the source's 3% downward axial-gradient correction and must be evaluated at their tabulated values. The current-study supplement contributes 21 numerical B8 volumes; one-peak detections have no volume and are excluded, while Figure 3 assigns +/-0.1 cm^3/mol plotting errors when two-peak uncertainties could not be constrained. Ozawa's printed Table 2 contributes 8 B8 P-V-T rows and is bundled at printed precision. Fischer's exact combined row selection and regression weights/objective are not printed. The source explicitly warns against extrapolating this EOS far beyond the B8 data range.

eos_records.label: Sun et al. (2019), liquid FeSiO3 2500 K BM4 reference

notes: This executable record is only the T0=2500 K BM4 reference term of the paper's larger P-V-T liquid model.

The paper classifies individual simulations from mean-square displacement. Figure 1 maps every Table 1 state to an unambiguous circle (liquid and used in the EOS fit) or square (nonliquid); the six square states are excluded by the bundled fit-selection flag.
The numerical pressure envelope summarizes the reported FPMD grid and is not a phase-stability guarantee.

eos_records.notes: The full source EOS adds a specialized thermal term built from a Gaussian heat-capacity function and a volume-dependent Gruneisen parameter. That thermal form is not currently represented by the eosmat schema, so this record deliberately stores only the explicitly defined, directly executable 2500 K BM4 reference isotherm. The exact 40-state liquid selection is bundled. The paper derives Cv from energy-temperature slopes and gamma from pressure-energy slopes before fitting their volume functions; the supporting information supplies those observations only as raster plots, whose regression-line slopes are now digitized in a separate dataset. The digitization closely recovers the published Cv function but cannot recover the authors' unknown relative weighting for the gamma function. Consequently, subtracting either rounded published or digitized thermal coefficients from Table 1 and freely fitting four BM4 coefficients remains an ill-conditioned sensitivity experiment, not a reproduction of the source regression.

numerical_reproduction.tolerance_basis: The printed one-standard-error uncertainty of the Table 1 pressure checkpoint.

state_classification.method: Match each exact Table 1 pressure-volume-temperature coordinate to the plotted marker shape; no coordinate is digitized or inferred from a subjective phase-boundary trace.

source_thermal_pressure_model.units: Cv in J/(mol K), V in cm^3/mol, and thermal pressure divided by 1000 to obtain GPa.

assessment.basis: Figure 1 resolves state membership exactly: the 40 circles are the liquid states used in the source fit and the six squares are excluded. Supporting Figures S3-S4 contain only high-resolution raster plots, but their regression-line slopes are digitized at nine volumes and reproduce the paper's stated Cv and gamma ranges. The digitized Cv function is close to the published Gaussian; the gamma polynomial remains sensitive to the unavailable source weighting. Subtracting either published or digitized thermal coefficients and freely fitting four BM4 parameters is nearly singular and hits the K0-double-prime audit bound. A stabilized check with V0 and K0-double-prime fixed recovers K0=2.24587 GPa and K0'=23.0422, but the unstable four-parameter sensitivity result must not be reported as a refitted EOS. Exact reproduction still requires the unrounded source values, constraints, weighting, and covariance treatment.

eos_records.label: Sokolova et al. (2013), Holzapfel thermal model (2016 workbook)
eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

This is not Miozzi's published EOS or a reproduction/correction of the original fit. V0,K0,K0_prime,gamma0,q fitted jointly; theta0=420 K, Tr=300 K, n=1 and two Fe atoms/cell fixed. Errors/covariance are conditional local standard errors using RSS/(131-5), assuming independent equal-variance pressure residuals. Calibrant systematics, shared/run correlations, predictor errors, fixed-theta uncertainty and model discrepancy are not included. Measured coverage is a marginal envelope, not a rectangular stability domain or validation for core-condition extrapolation.

notes: The fit combines Dewaele et al. (2012) room-temperature data with four new laser-heating experiments.
The KCl temperature is a modeled effective temperature below the measured Pt surface temperature; the bundled table stores the authors' KCl temperature.
The high-temperature calibration is experimental in pressure and volume but geometry-conditioned in temperature: it should not be interpreted as a homogeneous-temperature KCl thermodynamic dataset.

experimental_configuration.arrangement: Pt foil secured between two approximately 10 micrometer layers of dried KCl
experimental_configuration.temperature_convention: KCl diffraction samples a thermal gradient between the hot Pt surface and the approximately 295 K diamond anvils; the EOS uses the authors' estimated average KCl temperature

eos_records.notes: Nondefault Rydberg-Vinet alternative from Table I. Published V0=34.3(5) cm^3/mol converts to 56.956490004062935 A^3/B2 conventional cell with Z=1 and exact Avogadro constant. All five listed parameters are fitted; theta0=235 K, Tr=300 K, n=2 are held fixed. Fit includes all 123 Dewaele room-temperature rows and all 155 author-deposited Chidester effective-temperature rows. The integrated-Gruneisen Debye relation reproduces the complete fit. Dewaele and high-temperature Pt-derived pressures retain distinct calibration ancestry. KCl effective temperatures depend on the laser-heating gradient model; they are not directly measured homogeneous temperatures.

eos_records.label: Vocadlo (1999), static GGA BM3
eos_records.notes: Static-lattice GGA pseudopotential calculation for the named magnesite phase using a fully relaxed 30-atom MgCO3 cell (Z=6), with atomic positions and cell shape relaxed at nine volumes. The source reports the zero-pressure reference volume and an isothermal BM3 fit, but no finite-temperature or vibrational contribution; temperature_ref=0 K records that static electronic reference. The nine calculated states span -2.41596 to 207.419 GPa. Table 1 incorrectly labels both its energy and volume columns as per formula unit: its 160-295 A^3 volumes, stated V0=287.49 A^3, Figure 1 volume axis, and exact BM3 pressure reproduction establish the 30-atom conventional-cell basis; the energy rows likewise recover K0=98.921 GPa only when interpreted per 30-atom cell and give a factor-of-six error under the printed label. The parenthetical K0 and K0_prime errors are preserved, but the source states no confidence convention or covariance and gives no V0 uncertainty. The alternative K0_prime=4 fit, K0=111(1) GPa is not stored because the article calls it a poor second-order fit and does not use it in the subsequent analysis. The calculation finds no discontinuity within the sampled pressure range but explicitly cannot rule out reconstructive transitions with an energy barrier.

eos_records.notes: Preferred thermal parameterization from Table 1: a 300 K third-order Birch-Murnaghan reference isotherm plus quasi-harmonic Mie-Gruneisen-Debye thermal pressure. Equations 7-8 specify gamma=gamma0(V/V0)^q and theta=theta0*exp[-(gamma-gamma0)/q], which is Peritheos's integrated_gruneisen law, not the Fei et al. variable-exponent law used for the Pt calibrant. The source conventional-cell volumes are converted internally to molar volume using Z=6, while the public API remains in A^3 per conventional hexagonal cell. The paper also reports a separate high-temperature BM3 reference-state fit with alpha0, alpha1, and dK/dT; it is not represented here because the preferred MGD model is explicitly described as more reliable for extrapolation and is used in the downstream mantle calculations. The publication does not report the regression weights, residual definition, coefficient covariance, or confidence convention for parenthetical parameter errors. An independent unweighted pressure-residual refit is therefore a transparent reproduction diagnostic rather than a claim to duplicate the unpublished regression protocol.

notes: The authors call the specimen nominally (Mg0.22Fe0.78)O or Mw78, then use room-pressure synchrotron Mossbauer spectroscopy to resolve 71.6 mol% high-spin Fe2+, 4.6 mol% high-spin Fe3+, 21.5 mol% Mg, and 2.3 mol% net cation vacancies per O: Mg0.215Fe2+0.716Fe3+0.046□0.023O. The EOS records are attached to that defect-normalized measured composition because both DAC fragments came from the same characterized crystal. The Fm-3m sites are an average diffraction proxy: the final article explicitly says the nominal cubic cell and Bragg peaks do not fully describe the diffuse defect structure, and it does not publish an ordered defect-cluster refinement. Room-pressure Mossbauer data establish high-spin Fe2+ and Fe3+ only at ambient pressure; this study did not measure spin state under compression, so neither EOS record is labeled as a high-spin pressure branch. The neon crystal becomes increasingly hexagonally distorted above about 20 GPa under growing differential stress. That high-pressure indexing-cell fit is documented but excluded from execution because no space group or atomic structure is established.

cell_contents: Four nominal Mg0.5Fe0.5Al0.5Si0.5O3 formula units per conventional Pbnm bridgmanite cell (Z=4). All EOS volumes and bundled diffraction volumes use this 20-atom conventional-cell basis.
notes: Zhu et al. synthesized nominal FA50 from two runs whose recovered compositions were (Mg0.50Fe0.52)(Al0.47Si0.51)O3 and (Mg0.47Fe0.52)(Al0.46Si0.55)O3. The source does not map those two analyses to the individual XRD grains, so no grain-specific exact formula is inferred. Recovered material is LiNbO3-type at ambient conditions and converts to Pbnm bridgmanite above 18.8 GPa; consequently no ambient bridgmanite lattice or atom coordinates are fabricated here, and every V0 is a high-pressure-branch extrapolation. Sample 1 was stepwise laser annealed and develops a gradual mixed population of A-site high-spin and B-site low-spin Fe3+ through pressure-driven Fe-Al exchange. Sample 2 was cold compressed after its initial synthesis/anneal treatment and is the authors' reference for the original high-spin A-site ordering. The source supports no independently fitted, fully low-spin EOS branch.

The article reports the analytical/site-assigned composition (Mg0.88Fe3+0.065Fe2+0.035Al0.03)(Al0.11Si0.90)O3. notes: Composition-specific record for synthetic run 5K2667. The material formula preserves the article's measured Mg0.88Fe0.10Al0.14Si0.90O3 composition; the site-assigned form is (Mg0.88Fe3+0.065Fe2+0.035Al0.03)(Al0.11Si0.90)O3. The stored diffraction structure is the official deposited 4.2 GPa, 293 K Pbnm refinement with Z=4. Its normalized occupancies give Mg0.88Fe0.09Al0.13Si0.90O3, so it is a refinement model for the same specimen and not a replacement analytical composition. The EOS V0 values are separately fitted zero-pressure conventional-cell extrapolations. The authors report BM2 and BM3 as equally acceptable within uncertainty and do not designate a preferred fit; record ordering follows Table 1 and is not a scientific preference.

name: Bridgmanite

eos_records.label: Gong et al. (2004), shock-derived adiabatic BM3

notes: The coefficients define a zero-pressure reference isentrope reduced from high-temperature shock observations; 298.15 K is only the conventional numeric anchor for the reference state.

The first 47.75 GPa point is below the source's conservative >57.13 GPa perovskite assignment, and the source cautions that observations below 80 GPa may retain a small low-pressure-phase contribution.

eos_records.sample_composition: Natural Damaping enstatite, referred by the authors to (Mg0.92Fe0.08)SiO3; the reported oxide analysis includes minor Al, Ca, and other elements.
eos_records.notes: Accepted LitCurate source row 447. This equilibrium BM3 is the source's shock-reduced reference isentrope, not the directly measured principal Hugoniot and not an independently fitted 298 K isotherm. The AIP proceedings DOI 10.1063/1.1780510 repeats this same data set and is not represented as a second record.

parameter_provenance.determination_method: Measurements or their experimental reduction determine this EOS; source: Sections 2 and 3.3; Table 1.
parameter_provenance.equation: Section 3.3 explicitly derives a third-order Eulerian finite-strain (Birch-Murnaghan) isentrope from the porosity-corrected shock states using a Mie-Gruneisen reduction.
parameter_provenance.parameters: Section 3.3: K0S=260.1(9) GPa, K0S'=4.18(4), with rho0=4.19 g cm-3.
parameter_provenance.volume_basis: V0 is calculated as Z M/(rho0 N_A), with Z=4 and nominal molar mass 102.9102 g mol-1, giving 163.13738187176514 A3.
parameter_provenance.thermodynamic_basis: K0 and K0_prime are the source's adiabatic/isentrope coefficients K0S and K0S', not room-temperature isothermal K0T values. The schema's isothermal token denotes the executable equilibrium BM3 family because it has no separate adiabatic enum.

cell_contents: Four nominal Mg0.92Fe0.08SiO3 formula units per conventional orthorhombic perovskite cell (Z=4).
notes: The displayed Pbnm cell uses the established Fe-bearing bridgmanite axial ratios scaled isotropically to the density-derived EOS V0. It is a display cell, not a structure refinement of the chemically impure natural starting material. Gong et al. refer their analyzed natural pyroxene to the nominal Mg#92 formula used by this EOS record.

The positional model is a pure-MgSiO3 topology proxy, not a composition-bearing refinement.

primary_source_check.finding: The authors identify run 2 as CaFe2O4-type MgAl2O4 and construct a separate second-order Birch curve by fixing recovered V0, assuming K0'=4, and calculating K0 from one compressed cell. primary_data_check.finding: The complete observations used by the source construction are bundled from printed pressure and lattice values. There is exactly one informative finite-pressure state; the source reports no supplementary materials, and the audit found no associated repository series.

independent_refit.method: Analytical reproduction of the source's one-point construction: fixed recovered V0, K0'=4 implicit in BM2, and K0 equal to the normalized pressure of the rounded high-pressure lattice product.
independent_refit.finding: The analytically reconstructed K0 differs from the published value by 0.44 GPa because the printed axes are rounded. Applying the same calculation to the ruby/Pt pressure bracket gives a 6.01 GPa half-range, reproducing the published +/-6 GPa uncertainty after rounding; there is no independent regression residual test.

The source reports one-standard-deviation errors for V0 and the fitted adiabatic elastic quantities, but does not propagate the adopted thermodynamic constants into isothermal K0T/K0T' errors or publish covariance; those stored errors remain null rather than being inferred. numerical_reproduction.independent_acoustic_refit_check: An unweighted simultaneous nonlinear least-squares fit of Equations 1-2 to the ten decompression density/VP/VS rows plus the independently reported ambient density/VP/VS anchor gives K0S=163.5115 GPa, K0S'=4.21800, G0=129.7175 GPa, and G0'=2.43179 when using paragraph 10's explicit K0T-in-L2/M2 approximation for the measured isothermal strains. numerical_reproduction.limitation: Table 1 pressure was calculated from the same acoustic-derived BM3 and is not an independent pressure coordinate. Regressing those Pcal-V/V0 pairs would be circular and would also be limited by ratios printed to only three decimals. The paper does not state an observation-weighting rule or fitting software and describes an iterative adiabatic-foot correction without enough numerical detail to rerun it exactly. The deterministic ledger fit therefore uses paragraph 10's source-sanctioned K0T-in-L2/M2 approximation with ordinary unweighted velocity residuals. It directly reproduces the source's measurement-to-isothermal-coefficient chain, but it does not claim exact source covariance or a direct P-V regression.

eos_records.notes: This is the complete empirical pressure-scale form in Appendix B, not a standalone 300 K Vinet fit. Equation (3) and the three globally optimized coefficients define a zero-temperature cold Vinet curve; Equation (B2) adds an absolute thermal pressure that is nonzero at 300 K. The stored Tr=300 K is the Taylor expansion and operational increment reference, not the temperature of the cold curve. Tables II-III label compression by the ambient initial V0=1/rho0 from rho0=3.590 g/cm^3, whereas Equation (B2) defines eta with the smaller fitted cold V0K. The five new shock states span 152-265 GPa; four temperatures span 3088-5676 K and three Eulerian sound velocities are reported. The full quasi-Debye equations and inverse-variance objective are reconstructable from Luo et al. (2023) and Xian et al. (2022), and Peritheos implements that mechanism as SoundVelocityDebyeHelmholtz. The source-author numerical rerun is not reconstructable because the Kono velocity-density coefficients, complete upstream row mask, uncertainty propagation across P-V-T observables, and covariance are not published. A bounded 12-residual fit using only Luo Table I primary rows and a declared Li-2006 velocity-ratio proxy is recorded in the refit ledger; it does not replace this published Appendix-B record. No uncertainty confidence level or covariance is reported for the three optimized cold coefficients, and no errors are reported for c0-c5. The APS article record and full paper were checked; no official supplemental file or machine-readable data deposit is linked.

eos_records.label: Sokolova et al. (2013), Holzapfel thermal model (2016 workbook)
eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The implemented MgO a0 coefficient follows the explicit 2016 correction, so that term has dual 2013/2016 provenance. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

The implemented theta(V) relation follows exactly from d ln(theta)/d ln(V)=-gamma with gamma=gamma0(V/V0)^q, i.e. the integrated-Gruneisen law. Table 3's Murnaghan, Vinet, logarithmic, and alternate constrained BM3 fits are preserved separately as nonpreferred room-temperature model-sensitivity records; they are not thermal parameterizations. The static coefficients were obtained from a staged combined-data analysis that included earlier published room-temperature measurements; the bundled Table 2 contains all 61 new observations from this study. The K0' uncertainty is internally inconsistent: formal +/-0.06 in the text (0.05 after Table 3 rounding), pressure-propagated +/-0.2 in the text and abstract, and unexplained +/-0.3 in the conclusion; the stored +/-0.2 follows the explicit error analysis. No official supplement or machine-readable data deposit accompanies the article.

eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

scientific_validation.note: Equation and printed coefficients remain source-checked, but the Table II fit is not reproduced from the available published inputs. The published fixed-V0 NaCl-B2 Vinet curve gives 0.622381 GPa pressure RMS and mean residual -0.547610 GPa on 125 DAC-2 Table S1 observations above 35 GPa; all 125 residuals are negative. A direct unweighted refit gives K0=25.447259 GPa, K0_prime=5.582768 and RMS 0.293229 GPa, versus published 24.92 GPa and 5.63. The source-fit discrepancy is unresolved; including the above-33-GPa transition rows does not restore agreement.

(2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

notes: The article writes the analyzed composition as Al0.98(1)Si0.92(1)O3OH1.39(5). This is condensed hydroxyl notation for Al0.98Si0.92H1.39O4 (three O plus one O bearing 1.39 H), consistent with the official CIF analytical formula; it is not O4.39. The deposited 2018 X-ray structure fixes Al and Si occupancies to unity because refined and fixed-occupancy models were indistinguishable, and it contains no H atom site. The ideal fully occupied structural model therefore has Al4Si4H4O16 cell contents and is a diffraction model for the analyzed Al3.92Si3.68H5.56O16 composition, not an assertion that the measured vacancies or excess hydrogen were crystallographically resolved. The H coordinate is the powder-XRD position from Schmidt et al. (1998) explicitly used in the 2018 paper's Figure 1. The structural ambient volume, 214.431(13) A^3, differs from fitted V0 because the authors excluded the in-house ambient point from the synchrotron EOS regression. The Mookherjee et al. (2019) record uses the ideal nominal formula AlSiO3(OH); its EOS metadata remains record-specific. The ambient diffraction structure is Schmidt et al.'s ordered P21/n refinement: the seven fully occupied 4e sites give four AlSiO4H formula units and the reported lattice gives 212.99 A^3. P21/n is the alternate setting of P21/c (space-group number 14). The structural volume is intentionally distinct from the static-DFT LP EOS reference volume of 210.21 A^3. Phase D is a different composition and material in the catalog.

eos_records.label: Holmes et al. (1989), theoretical 300 K Vinet scale
eos_records.notes: The 300 K pressure scale is Holmes et al.'s theoretical universal (Vinet) EOS, qualified against shock data to at least 10% in pressure. Equation (11) and Table IV give V0=101.9 bohr^3/atom, P_T=798.31 GPa, and eta=7.2119; the executable Vinet coefficients are the exact mappings K0=P_T/3 and K0'=1+eta/1.5. Table IV's separately printed B_T=266 GPa and B_T'=5.81 are rounded interpretations of the same curve. The approximate finite-temperature extension adds alpha*B_T*(T-300 K), with alpha=0.261e-4 K^-1 and rounded B_T=266 GPa, and is stated to be adequate below 2000 K. The 300 K isotherm itself is represented through 550 GPa; 32-660 GPa is the shock-Hugoniot range, not the static-isotherm validity range. The source publishes no numerical LMTO E0(V), P0(V), density-of-states, or 300 K fit grid, so the analytical curve is exactly reconstructable but its underlying theoretical fit is not independently refittable.

eos_records.notes: Diagnostic reconstruction of Yokoo (2009) Table V calculated PVT outputs; published analytical PVT remains unreproduced. Not a validated replacement for the source pressure standard. Cold BM3 V0 is Vc at 0 K; ambient normalization is Vc/cold_volume_ratio. Phonon and electronic pressures are absolute relative to 0 K. Numerical bounds do not guarantee solid Au/Pt throughout the rectangular domain; use the source phase markers. Pt has an additional derived residual-pressure correction, linear between source temperatures, retained separately from the original electronic table. Its physical origin is unresolved. No parameter errors or covariance are inferred from model-output residuals. This pressure model supplies no caloric potential.

eos_records.label: Sokolova et al. (2013), Holzapfel thermal model (2016 workbook)
eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

eos_records.label: Wang et al. (2012), principal Vinet-MGD presentation
eos_records.notes: This is a thermal EOS, not a standalone room-temperature Vinet fit. Equations 1 and 4-8 add a Debye Mie-Gruneisen pressure increment relative to 300 K; with a=1, gamma(V)=gamma0*(V/V0)^b and theta(V)=theta0*exp[-gamma0*((V/V0)^b-1)/b]. The paper also reports an equally successful BM3-MGD alternative: V0=46.55 A^3 fixed, K0=294(2) GPa, K0'=4.85(12), theta0=1130(100) K, gamma0=1.66(7), a=1 fixed, and b=2.9(4). Vinet is retained as the single executable record from this paper because Figure 2 uses it and Tables 3-4 present its values first, with BM3 in parentheses; the authors state that the two fits agree within analytical uncertainty rather than explicitly designating a preferred model. The fixed V0 rounds the independently measured recovered-sample value 46.553(19) A^3; null in parameter_errors means it was not a fitted coefficient, not that the ambient measurement lacked uncertainty. Several measurements crossed the established stishovite-CaCl2-type boundary without transforming on the experimental timescale; the authors report that excluding them gives identical fit results, so the marginal P-T envelope is not a rectangular phase-stability claim.

eos_records.label: Sokolova et al. (2013), Holzapfel thermal model (2016 workbook)
eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.

eos_records.notes: This record uses the self-consistent Sokolova et al. (2013) pressure-scale fit: Table 1 supplies reference volume/composition inputs and Table 4 supplies the final Holzapfel and thermal coefficients. The fit jointly considers shock-wave, ultrasonic, X-ray diffraction, dilatometric, and thermochemical measurements; it is not derived from one experimental dataset. Sokolova et al. (2016) republishes the parameters and supplies the executable Excel/VBA implementation, reference-temperature convention, and corrected equations, rather than a new fit dataset. The publications do not provide individual parameter errors, parameter covariance, or a complete machine-readable list of fit points and weights. A source-constrained reconstruction nevertheless combines 392 room-temperature comparison observations for all eleven markers in one shared Equation (20) objective against the pointwise mean of the precursor Table 2 Holzapfel and Table 3 Vinet isotherms, with Table 4 retained as a post-calibration closure test. This tests the coupled cross-calibration and is not an independent refit of the eleven EOS coefficient sets. The *_sokolova_2013 identifier names the scientific fit year; the 2016 workbook remains explicit in source_lineage as the implementation and correction source.
